Although the evaluation setting is public ledgers, the formalism and invariants apply to any probabilistic agent acting on irreversible external state.
tldr: This paper formalizes safety invariants for agents performing irreversible state transitions on public ledgers, proving execution fidelity under a fault model.
motivation: Existing agent frameworks optimize task success but neglect safety of irreversible side-effects, motivating a formal approach to guarantee correct execution.
method: The authors model ledger value movement as state transitions in a four-dimensional space and derive seven safety invariants from a fidelity condition, then evaluate on an adversarial suite.
result: The stack improves pass rate by ~74 points on write-aggressive models but only ~3 on a write-cautious one, with 108 production operations supporting the taxonomy.
conclusion: The formalism and invariants apply broadly to probabilistic agents acting on irreversible external state, but the paper is not aligned with the user's quantum information research interests.

title: Block Sensitivity Can Exceed Spectral Sensitivity Squared
authors: Alexander Meiburg
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spectral sensitivity [MATH] of a Boolean function is the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of its sensitivity graph. It lower-bounds every standard measure of query complexity, and Aaronson, Ben-David, Kothari, Rao and Tal, who introduced it, asked whether block sensitivity is at most quadratic in it: is [MATH]? We show that it is not. We construct a total Boolean function on [MATH] variables with [MATH] and [MATH], so that [MATH], and hence by composition a family with [MATH] and [MATH]. The function is the indicator of a union of [MATH] subcubes indexed by the vertices of a doubly regular tournament, and the freedom left in the construction is fixed by the Lov\'asz local lemma. The main result has been formally verified in Lean. We also give numerical evidence that a member of the same family on [MATH] variables reaches an exponent near [MATH], and exhibit a member on [MATH] variables whose exponent already exceeds [MATH] and whose spectral sensitivity can be computed exactly.
tldr: This paper disproves a conjecture about the relationship between block sensitivity and spectral sensitivity of Boolean functions, a result in classical computational complexity.
motivation: The paper addresses an open question in Boolean function complexity theory, specifically whether block sensitivity is at most quadratic in spectral sensitivity, which has implications for query complexity lower bounds.
method: The authors construct a total Boolean function based on a union of subcubes indexed by a doubly regular tournament, using the Lovász local lemma to fix parameters, and verify the main result in the Lean proof assistant.
result: They show that block sensitivity can exceed spectral sensitivity squared, providing a counterexample to the conjecture and a family of functions with a larger exponent.
conclusion: The result refutes the quadratic relationship, indicating that spectral sensitivity does not tightly bound block sensitivity, which may impact the understanding of query complexity measures.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Participation Governance For Verifiable Ai Agents In Open Digital Twin Ecosystems
authors: Juan Li, Wei Cai, Yan Bai
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous AI agents, increasingly empowered by large language models, are becoming important components of human-machine systems for high-stakes decision support in digital twin ecosystems. However, existing multi-agent systems often lack robust verification for identity, capability, and policy compliance, especially in decentralized environments spanning multiple institutions. This paper proposes a neuro-symbolic decentralized governance framework for verifiable agents in collaborative digital twin environments. By representing agents through multi-layer semantic profiles, the framework bridges probabilistic neural reasoning with deterministic institutional governance, thereby supporting trustworthy human-AI collaboration and meaningful human oversight. Capabilities are grounded in formal domain ontologies to enable machine-interpretable, policy-aware, and context-sensitive participation. These credentials, issued by organizational authorities, are validated via blockchain-based smart contracts, ensuring auditable participation without exposing sensitive data. We demonstrate the framework using a decision-support prototype with clinic, digital twin, and wearable provider agents effectively prevents unauthorized interaction and enforces institutional policies with manageable overhead. Our findings suggest that neuro-symbolic decentralized governance provides a scalable and trustworthy pathway for safe human-machine collaboration across institutional boundaries.
tldr: This paper proposes a neuro-symbolic decentralized governance framework for verifiable AI agents in digital twin ecosystems, using semantic profiles and blockchain-based credentials.
motivation: Existing multi-agent systems lack robust verification for identity, capability, and policy compliance in decentralized environments, hindering trustworthy human-AI collaboration.
method: The framework represents agents via multi-layer semantic profiles grounded in domain ontologies, and validates credentials through blockchain-based smart contracts.
result: A decision-support prototype with clinic, digital twin, and wearable provider agents prevents unauthorized interaction and enforces institutional policies with manageable overhead.
conclusion: Neuro-symbolic decentralized governance offers a scalable and trustworthy pathway for safe human-machine collaboration across institutional boundaries.

title: NoisePQC++: A Unified NIST-Compliant Pqc And Hybrid-PQC Implementation Of The Noise Protocol
authors: Nadeem Ahmed, Aryya Gangopadhyay, Lei Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The threat of quantum computers to classical public-key cryptography has created an urgent need to evolve secure communication protocols with post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) primitives. The Noise Protocol Framework, widely used in systems such as WireGuard and WhatsApp, traditionally relies on the Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) public-key exchange scheme, which is vulnerable to quantum threats. In this paper, we present NoisePQC++, a unified C++23 implementation of the Noise Protocol framework augmented with post-quantum Key Encapsulation Mechanisms and Hybrid Forward Secrecy. Our design integrates the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) standardized ML-KEM algorithm alongside classical ECDH, enabling full PQC, hybrid ECDH+PQC handshakes, and unified support for all 57 classical Noise handshake pattern variants, 13 post-quantum Noise handshakes, and their hybrid variants. Compared with prior work, NoisePQC++ offers broader protocol coverage, more complete implementation support, and greater flexibility. Our evaluation shows minimal overhead under normal network conditions and acceptable overhead in adverse cases, while significantly improving resistance against quantum adversaries. These results indicate that NIST-standardized post-quantum and hybrid Noise handshakes are practical and provide a credible basis for future deployment.
tldr: This paper presents a C++ implementation of the Noise Protocol Framework with post-quantum and hybrid key exchange, but it is primarily a software engineering effort with no new information-theoretic or physical insights.
motivation: The threat of quantum computers to classical public-key cryptography motivates integrating NIST-standardized post-quantum algorithms into secure communication protocols like the Noise Protocol Framework.
method: The authors implement NoisePQC++, a C++23 library that integrates ML-KEM with classical ECDH, supporting all 57 classical Noise handshake patterns, 13 post-quantum handshakes, and hybrid variants.
result: The implementation shows minimal overhead under normal network conditions and acceptable overhead in adverse cases, while improving resistance against quantum adversaries.
conclusion: The paper concludes that NIST-standardized post-quantum and hybrid Noise handshakes are practical and provide a credible basis for future deployment.

authors: Michael Te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:

Active matter has become a lively topic in recent years, but what exactly is meant by the term ‘active matter’ is often unclear. This Colloquium discusses the scientific and semantic issues underlying this ambiguity, as well as the history of the field, and offers a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems. It then surveys recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 031001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review covers tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution, a technique in nanoscale optical imaging.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize recent advances in tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy, which combines scanning probe techniques with optical fluorescence to achieve superresolution beyond the diffraction limit.
method: The review discusses the principles of using a scanning tip as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine electromagnetic fields, and surveys experimental techniques and insights from the field.
result: The review highlights that atomic-scale resolution in fluorescence microscopy is achievable, enabling the study of molecular electronic and vibronic properties at the submolecular level.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy is a powerful tool for nanoscale imaging and spectroscopy, with potential applications in molecular identification and reaction studies.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This review paper discusses the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Understanding vacuum breakdown is crucial for improving the reliability and efficiency of particle accelerators and other high-power technologies.
method: The paper synthesizes recent experimental and simulation studies to present a coherent mechanistic picture of breakdown initiation.
result: It identifies key factors such as surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles that interact to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: Insights from this review could lead to better design of high-power devices and more reliable advanced accelerators.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications, including magnetism, topology, and dynamics.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnets, covering topics like ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism, topology, and nonequilibrium dynamics.
result: The review highlights the rapid evolution of the field, including new materials, experimental techniques, and potential applications in spintronics and other areas.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are a rich field with many open questions and promising applications, but the paper does not directly contribute to the user's specific research directions.

authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:

This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars with future detectors and emphasizes multimessenger observations.
motivation: The paper aims to highlight the scientific potential of continuous gravitational wave searches and their connection to electromagnetic astronomy and nuclear astrophysics.
method: It is a review article that surveys detection prospects, detector capabilities, and the implications of multimessenger observations.
result: The paper discusses the expected sensitivity of future detectors and the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations for source identification and physics extraction.
conclusion: Continuous gravitational wave astronomy offers a unique window into dense matter physics, and future detectors will enhance multimessenger opportunities.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the kagome lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind the wealth of exotic phenomena observed in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and orbital antiferromagnetism.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, discussing the role of frustration, interference effects, and spin-orbit coupling.
result: It highlights the emergence of topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and various correlated states, and discusses their implications.
conclusion: Kagome metals provide a rich platform for exploring strongly correlated and topological physics, but the review does not directly contribute to the user's specified research directions.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for chemical, ecological, and epidemiological modeling.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for analyzing complex systems modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, which are prevalent in biology, sociology, and physics.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic techniques, such as path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism, to derive and solve stochastic reaction-diffusion equations.
result: The review demonstrates how field-theoretic methods can systematically handle nonlinearities and fluctuations in reaction-diffusion systems, offering a coherent perspective across disciplines.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are powerful tools for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, but the paper is a pedagogical review without novel contributions to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research, emphasizing the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes findings from experiments, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations in spin-glass systems.
result: It tracks the progress in understanding spin-glass dynamics and highlights future research opportunities.
conclusion: The review underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration in advancing spin-glass physics.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic states of matter with potential applications in quantum computing, but their realization in materials is challenging.
method: The review synthesizes theoretical models (Kitaev model) and experimental findings on candidate materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The paper provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of Kitaev spin liquid research, identifying promising materials and open questions.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with potential for topological quantum computation, but further experimental and theoretical work is needed to confirm and utilize these states.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review connects statistical physics methods (maximum entropy, renormalization group) to large-scale neural recordings, aiming to uncover reproducible collective behaviors in brain networks.
motivation: The authors aim to bridge quantitative neuroscience experiments with theoretical physics principles, seeking predictive power in brain studies akin to other physics areas.
method: The paper reviews recent progress, discussing maximum entropy models and renormalization group approaches applied to simultaneous recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: The review highlights new reproducible behaviors in neural networks and demonstrates that abstract theoretical principles can have predictive power in neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for understanding collective neural dynamics, with potential for deeper insights into brain function.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on photophysical processes.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical approaches to internal conversion, which is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models and methods used to describe nonradiative transitions in quantum systems.
result: The review summarizes the state of the art and discusses how these methods can be applied to relevant applications.
conclusion: The authors conclude that these theoretical methods are crucial for understanding and optimizing photophysical processes in quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their formation and quantum features.
motivation: To provide an overview of quantum-mechanical properties of magnetic skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics and quantum technologies.
method: The paper is a review article summarizing theoretical and experimental work on quantum interactions underlying skyrmion formation and quantum characteristics of skyrmions themselves.
result: It discusses how quantum effects influence skyrmion stability, dynamics, and potential quantum functionalities.
conclusion: The review highlights open questions and future directions for exploiting quantum properties of skyrmions in technology.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, potentially mediated by new bosons and linked to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To consolidate the state of the art in searches for new spin-dependent forces, which could reveal physics beyond the Standard Model and shed light on dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper is a review, summarizing theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and surveying experimental techniques and results from various precision measurement experiments.
result: The review catalogs numerous experimental bounds and theoretical models for spin-dependent exotic interactions, highlighting the current status and future prospects.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, with ongoing and future experiments expected to improve sensitivity.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances, but is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The paper aims to review the state of the art in theoretical nuclear astrophysics, addressing the challenge of measuring low-energy stellar reactions in the lab.
method: It provides a comprehensive review of quantum-mechanical phenomena such as tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects in stellar nuclear reactions.
result: The review consolidates current theoretical approaches and discusses new ideas for experimental study of these reactions on Earth.
conclusion: The paper is a valuable resource for nuclear astrophysics but does not align with the specified research interests.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining that apparent violations arise from violating assumptions in the bounds' derivations.
motivation: To clarify why some measured material properties exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how such violations can be exploited to design novel materials.
method: A review of various physical properties and circumstances where measurements exceed thermodynamic bounds, analyzing which underlying assumptions are violated.
result: Identifies multiple cases where bounds are exceeded due to assumptions like equilibrium, homogeneity, or linearity being violated, and discusses how to engineer materials to achieve such properties.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but stem from misapplied assumptions; understanding this enables the design of materials with extreme properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical implementations of synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries such as fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions.
motivation: To survey recent advances in simulating exotic geometries with atomic, photonic, and electronic systems, which could enable studies of topology and gravity analogs.
method: The paper is a review (Colloquium) that synthesizes results from multiple platforms and theoretical models.
result: It highlights how nonstandard geometries can be realized and used to explore novel quantum phenomena.
conclusion: The field is promising for quantum simulation but is not directly aligned with the user's specific research directions.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: This review paper discusses self-alignment in active matter systems, a topic in soft matter physics with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to unify and review the concept of self-alignment in active matter, which is a key mechanism in biological and robotic systems, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests.
method: The paper provides a conceptual and mathematical framework for self-alignment, reviews existing models, and discusses applications in biology, smart materials, and robotics.
result: The review highlights how self-alignment leads to novel collective behaviors and offers a unified perspective on active systems.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a powerful principle in active matter with broad implications, but it does not align with the user's focus on quantum information and related fields.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: This review paper discusses experimental and theoretical efforts to probe gravity using massive quantum systems, focusing on decoherence and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: The authors aim to review the state-of-the-art in testing gravity with quantum systems, as classical gravity is poorly tested and quantum probes may reveal new physics.
method: The paper is a review, summarizing theoretical models and experimental proposals for observing gravitational effects on quantum superpositions and entanglement.
result: It highlights ongoing experiments and theoretical frameworks that could determine whether gravity induces decoherence or can entangle massive particles.
conclusion: The review concludes that such experiments are feasible and will guide future theories of quantum gravity.

title: Converting P T -symmetric Topological Classes By Floquet En...
authors: Ming-Jian Gao And Jun-Hong An
abstract: Going beyond the conventional classification rule of Altland-Zirnbauer symmetry classes, symmetric topological phases are classified by or . The interconversion between the two -symmetric topological classes is generally difficult due to the constraint of . Here, we propose a scheme to control and interconvert the -symmetric topological classes by Floquet engineering. We find that it is the removal of the gauge degree of freedom, induced by the phase difference between different hopping rates, by the periodic driving that leads to such an interconversion. Relaxing the system from the constraint of , rich exotic topological phases, e.g. the coexisting -symmetric first-order real Chern insulator and second-order topological insulator not only in different quasienergy gaps, but also in one single gap, are generated. In contrast to conventional Floquet topological phases, our result provides a way to realize exotic topological phases without changing symmetries. It enriches the family of topological phases and gives an insightful guidance for the development of multifunctional quantum devices.
tldr: This paper proposes a Floquet engineering scheme to interconvert PT-symmetric topological classes, generating exotic topological phases without changing symmetries.
motivation: The interconversion between PT-symmetric topological classes is difficult due to symmetry constraints, and the authors aim to control this via periodic driving.
method: They use Floquet engineering to remove a gauge degree of freedom induced by phase differences in hopping rates, enabling topological class interconversion.
result: They generate coexisting PT-symmetric first-order real Chern insulator and second-order topological insulator in different quasienergy gaps and even in a single gap.
conclusion: The work enriches topological phases and provides guidance for multifunctional quantum devices, but it is not aligned with the user's research interests.

title: Structural Signatures Of Memory In Amorphous Solids
authors: Dor Shohat And Yoav Lahini Ori Engel
abstract: Amorphous materials can retain memories of past deformations, offering a pathway to understanding their complex energy landscape and self-organization dynamics. These memories are stored in the physical structure; however, reading them from a static structural snapshot remains a challenge and current memory readout protocols rely on dynamic, memory erasing measurements. Here we study several coarse-grained models of amorphous solids with increasing complexity, and demonstrate that the memory of a deformation amplitude can be retrieved from a single structural order parameter. We start from an abstract collection of non-interacting bi-stable elements, where the relation between memory and structural configuration is derived analytically. Using theoretical arguments and numerical simulations, we extend this framework to interacting systems, including one-dimensional chains and two-dimensional networks of coupled bi-stable elements. In the latter case, the order parameter depends on the geometry of the memorized drive. These results point to a general and minimal framework for non-destructive memory retrieval in amorphous materials, from a static snapshot of their internal structure or stress distribution.
tldr: This paper studies memory in amorphous solids using coarse-grained models, showing that deformation amplitude can be retrieved from a static structural order parameter.
motivation: To understand memory storage in amorphous materials and enable non-destructive readout from static snapshots, which is currently challenging.
method: The authors analyze abstract non-interacting bi-stable elements analytically, then extend to interacting systems (1D chains and 2D networks) via theory and simulations.
result: They demonstrate that a single structural order parameter can retrieve deformation amplitude, with geometry dependence in 2D networks.
conclusion: The work provides a minimal framework for non-destructive memory retrieval in amorphous solids, but it is unrelated to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Memory Of Topologically Constrained Disorder In Shakti Artificial Spin Ice
authors: Cristiano Nisoli And Yair Shokef Priyanka Priyanka
abstract: Complex behaviors often sit at a critical threshold between order and disorder. But not all disorder is created equal. Disorder can be trivial or constrained, and correlated disorder can even be topological. Crucially, constrained disorder can harbor memory, leading to non-trivial, sequence-dependent responses to external manipulations. And yet the fascinating subject of ‘memory of disorder’ remains poorly explored, as memory is often associated to the retention of metastable order. In recent years artificial frustrated materials—in particular arrays of frustrated nanomagnets known as artificial spin ices—have been employed to study complex disorders and its wealth of exotic behaviors, yet their memory properties have received much less attention. Here, we investigate both analytically and numerically the sequence-dependent responses of two somehow opposite yet related artificial spin ices: the Landau-ordered square spin ice and the disordered but topologically-ordered Shakti spin ice. We find that Shakti exhibits a pronounced sequence-dependent response, whereas in the square lattice, such path dependence is absent. Within Shakti, even the minimal periodic supercell demonstrates both deterministic and stochastic forms of sequence memory, depending on the interaction strength. Extending our study to cyclic driving, we find that retracing the same input path leads to enhanced memory retention. These results open new perspectives on how topological constraints and correlated disorder generate robust memory effects in frustrated artificial materials, hitherto examined mainly in terms of their ground-state kinetics and thermodynamics.
tldr: This paper studies memory effects in artificial spin ices, focusing on topological constraints and disorder, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to explore how topological constraints and correlated disorder generate robust memory effects in frustrated artificial materials, which have been studied mainly for ground-state kinetics and thermodynamics.
method: They analytically and numerically investigate sequence-dependent responses in two artificial spin ices: Landau-ordered square spin ice and disordered Shakti spin ice, including cyclic driving.
result: Shakti exhibits pronounced sequence-dependent memory, while square ice does not; even minimal supercells show deterministic and stochastic memory depending on interaction strength.
conclusion: Topological constraints and correlated disorder can produce robust memory effects in artificial frustrated materials, opening new perspectives for memory applications.

title: Topological Evolution Of Band Degeneracies And Bound States In The Continuum In Anisotropic Photonic Crystal Slabs
authors: Xin Gao, Ze-Huan Zheng, Qilin Duan, Huanyang Chen And Ying Chen
abstract: Topological degeneracies, such as Dirac or Weyl points and exceptional points, play a vital role in photonics and metamaterials due to their unique topological characteristics. This study investigates the intricate evolution of topological charges in degenerate bands, focusing on the interactions among bound states in the continuum (BICs), degenerate states (DS) and circularly polarized states (C points). Specifically, by controlling the optical axis (OA) orientation in anisotropic materials to break azimuthal anisotropy symmetry, we elucidate the evolutionary laws of DS and BICs in momentum space with the rotation of OA, and clarify the accompanying phenomena of charge annihilation and generation. When polar anisotropy symmetry is broken, the complex processes including splitting of BICs, migration of C points and the charge reversal of Γ-point BICs are further displayed. Our work introduces an additional degree of freedom for modulating band degeneracies and their associated topological properties, inspiring future developments in singularity physics through engineering naturally anisotropic materials.
tldr: This paper studies topological charges and bound states in the continuum in anisotropic photonic crystal slabs, focusing on band degeneracies and their evolution with symmetry breaking.
motivation: The authors aim to understand and control topological degeneracies (Dirac/Weyl points, exceptional points) in photonic systems, which are important for photonics and metamaterials.
method: They theoretically analyze anisotropic photonic crystal slabs, varying the optical axis orientation to break azimuthal and polar anisotropy symmetries, and track the evolution of topological charges, BICs, and C points in momentum space.
result: They reveal evolutionary laws for degenerate states and BICs under symmetry breaking, including charge annihilation/generation, splitting of BICs, migration of C points, and charge reversal at the Γ point.
conclusion: The work introduces a new degree of freedom for modulating band degeneracies and topological properties, potentially inspiring future developments in singularity physics using naturally anisotropic materials.

title: Probing Quark Electromagnetic Properties Via Entangled Quark Pairs In Fragmentation Hadrons At Lepton Colliders
authors: Qing-Hong Cao, Guanghui Li, Xin-Kai Wen And Bin Yan
abstract: Electromagnetic dipole interactions of light quarks induce distinct spin correlations in quark pairs produced at lepton colliders, favoring entangled spin-triplet state aligned along the axis or spin-singlet state. These correlations lead to unique azimuthal asymmetries in inclusive -dihadron pair production and in back-to-back hadron pairs ( ), which are absent in the SM. Using published Belle and BaBar measurements together with projected sensitivities based on ratios of azimuthal asymmetries, we demonstrate that these measurements provide significant constraints on light-quark dipole couplings, with a reduced dependence on poorly known nonperturbative fragmentation functions and free from contamination by other new physics effects. This approach offers a clean and novel probe of light-quark dipole interactions in collider experiments.
tldr: This paper proposes using spin correlations in entangled quark pairs from lepton colliders to probe light-quark electromagnetic dipole moments, but it is a high-energy physics phenomenology study with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to find a clean probe of light-quark dipole couplings, which are poorly constrained and could indicate new physics beyond the Standard Model.
method: They analyze spin correlations in quark-antiquark pairs produced at lepton colliders, focusing on azimuthal asymmetries in dihadron production, and use Belle/BaBar data plus projected sensitivities to constrain dipole couplings.
result: The proposed asymmetries provide significant constraints on light-quark dipole couplings with reduced dependence on fragmentation functions and no contamination from other new physics.
conclusion: This offers a novel collider probe of quark dipole interactions, but it is not relevant to the specified research directions.

title: El Agente Cuántico: Automating Quantum Simulations
authors: Ignacio Gustin, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Juan B Pérez-Sánchez, Chris Crebolder, Jérôme F Gonthier, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Yuma Nakamura, Karthik Panicker, Manav Ramprasad, Aiwei Yin, Zijian Zhang, Yunheng Zou, Varinia Bernales And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract: Quantum simulation is central to understanding and designing quantum systems across physics and chemistry. However, its practical use is often limited by the exponential growth of Hilbert space and by the increasing complexity of modern quantum-simulation software. Here we introduce El Agente Cuántico, a multi-agent AI system that automates quantum-simulation workflows by translating natural-language scientific intent into executed and validated computations across heterogeneous quantum-software frameworks. By reasoning directly over library documentation and APIs, our agentic system dynamically assembles end-to-end simulations spanning—but not limited to—state preparation, closed- and open-system dynamics, tensor-network methods, quantum control, quantum error correction, and quantum resource estimation. The developed system unifies traditionally distinct simulation paradigms behind a single natural-language interface. Beyond reducing technical barriers, this approach opens a path toward scalable, adaptive, and increasingly autonomous quantum simulation, enabling faster exploration of physical models, rapid hypothesis testing, and closer integration between theory, simulation, and emerging quantum hardware.
tldr: This paper introduces an AI agent system for automating quantum simulations via natural language, but it does not align with the specified research directions.
motivation: Quantum simulation is limited by Hilbert space growth and software complexity, motivating an automated system to lower barriers.
method: The system uses multi-agent AI to translate natural language into executable quantum simulation workflows across various software frameworks.
result: It demonstrates automated end-to-end simulations including state preparation, dynamics, tensor networks, and error correction.
conclusion: The approach aims to make quantum simulation more accessible and adaptive, but it is not a core contribution to the listed research areas.

title: From Intuition To Optimization: A Review Of Inverse Design Applied To Optical Nanotweezers
authors: Sejeong Kim And Kenneth B Crozier Damian Nelson
abstract: Optical nanotweezers, which integrate nanophotonic structures such as plasmonic antennas, dielectric resonators, and metasurfaces, have emerged as powerful tools for manipulating nanoparticles, biomolecules, and viruses with high precision. However, traditional designs rely heavily on heuristic approaches and simple geometries, limiting performance. Inverse design offers a paradigm shift by using computational optimization methods to discover non-intuitive, high-performance structures for optical trapping. This review provides an overview of key inverse design methodologies, including adjoint-based optimization, topology optimization, and machine learning approaches, and highlights their broader impact across nanophotonics. We then focus on their application to optical nanotweezers, where recent advances demonstrate enhanced trapping stiffness, reduced optical heating, and tailored trapping landscapes. Representative examples include algorithmic design of plasmonic nanotweezers, topology-optimized plasmonic nanoapertures, inverse-designed dielectric nanocavities, and force-centric designs based on Maxwell stress tensor engineering. Collectively, these studies illustrate how inverse design enables stable, efficient, and versatile optical trapping at the nanoscale. Despite these advances, challenges remain in fabrication, computational cost, and the interpretability of optimized structures. We conclude with a perspective on future directions, emphasizing opportunities in reconfigurable tweezers, lab-on-a-chip integration, and quantum nanophotonics. By bridging photonic optimization with nanoscale manipulation, inverse-designed optical nanotweezers offer promising opportunities for future applications in biophysics, materials science, and quantum technologies.
tldr: A review of inverse design methods for optical nanotweezers, focusing on computational optimization for nanophotonic trapping structures.
motivation: Traditional optical nanotweezer designs rely on heuristics and simple geometries, limiting performance; inverse design offers a path to optimized, non-intuitive structures.
method: The paper reviews inverse design methodologies including adjoint-based optimization, topology optimization, and machine learning, and surveys their application to optical nanotweezers.
result: Recent advances demonstrate enhanced trapping stiffness, reduced heating, and tailored trapping landscapes, with examples like topology-optimized nanoapertures and force-centric designs.
conclusion: Inverse-designed optical nanotweezers hold promise for biophysics, materials science, and quantum technologies, but challenges in fabrication, computational cost, and interpretability remain.

title: Review On Band Structure And Spin Polarization Of Altermagnetic Materials
authors: Xiangnan Xie, Xiaoyue He, Fayuan Zhang And Chaoyu Chen
abstract: Recent theoretical and experimental efforts have revealed the existence of a new class of magnetic materials, altermagnets, characterized by distinct symmetries in spin and real space. Combining the properties of ferromagnets, such as band spin polarization and time-reversal symmetry breaking responses, and antiferromagnets, like vanishing stray field and terahertz magnon dynamics, altermagnets are attracting enormous attention in both magnetism and spintronics community. While numerous altermagnetic candidates and emerging physical properties have been studied in theory extensively and enthusiastically, the experimental investigation of altermagnetism is struggling against the lack of proper altermagnetic materials and the controversial results reported for specific candidates. In this review, we first give a general description on the concept and key properties of altermagnetism, outline its distinction from other compensated magnetic order from the aspects of time-reversal symmetry in the spin momentum locking texture and time-reversal symmetry breaking responses. The main body of this review concentrates on the progress in altermagnetic material study with special focus on their band structure and spin polarization features, as well as the controversies over several candidate materials. Going forward, we point out several directions which altermagnetic material investigation might follow and guidelines which could help to avoid the pitfalls in the experimental pursuit of ideal altermagnets.
tldr: A review of altermagnetic materials focusing on their band structure and spin polarization, highlighting experimental challenges and controversies.
motivation: To provide an overview of altermagnetism, a new class of magnetic materials, and to address the lack of proper materials and controversial experimental results.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental progress on altermagnetic materials, emphasizing band structure and spin polarization features, and discusses controversies and future directions.
result: Summarizes key properties of altermagnets, distinguishes them from other magnetic orders, and identifies pitfalls in experimental pursuit.
conclusion: Altermagnetic materials show promise for spintronics, but experimental verification is challenging; guidelines are provided for future investigation.

title: Switchable Band Alignment In 2D-perovskite/WS2 Heterostructures For Tunable Exciton Transport And Valley Polarization
authors: Yingying Chen, Zeyi Liu, Zisheng Gong, Cheng Wang, Wendian Yao, Junze Li, Ti Wang, Weibo Gao And Dehui Li
abstract: Van der Waals heterostructures integrated by two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) hold great potential for engineering promising exciton phenomena, particularly interlayer excitons (IXs) featuring extended lifetimes and permanent out-of-plane electric dipole moments. While electrically controllable IX emission has been extensively explored in TMD heterobilayers, reconfiguring their band alignment to achieve selected exciton states and exploit these states for novel excitonic functionalities remains an urgent challenge. Here, we demonstrate dynamic exciton control by electrically tunable band alignment transitions between type-II and type-I configurations in WS2/(iso-BA)2PbI4 heterostructures, enabling reversible conversion between charged interlayer (IX±) and charged intralayer (X−) excitons. By tailoring these exciton states, we achieve two critical functionalities: (i) 7 μm ON/OFF control of exciton transport via transition between delocalized IX± (ON) and confined X− (OFF) states; (ii) valley polarization switching with a 16.3 ON/OFF ratio, leveraging distinct spin-valley configurations of IX± (unpolarized) and X− (polarized). Unlike twist-angle-dependent TMD heterobilayers, this platform operates independently of stacking alignment, establishing a broadly hybrid 2D system as a practical paradigm towards programmable nanophotonic circuits.
tldr: This paper demonstrates electrically tunable band alignment in 2D perovskite/WS2 heterostructures to control exciton transport and valley polarization.
motivation: To achieve dynamic control of exciton states and functionalities in van der Waals heterostructures, overcoming limitations of twist-angle-dependent TMD bilayers.
method: They fabricate WS2/(iso-BA)2PbI4 heterostructures and apply electric fields to switch between type-II and type-I band alignments, converting between charged interlayer and intralayer excitons.
result: They achieve 7 μm ON/OFF control of exciton transport and valley polarization switching with a 16.3 ON/OFF ratio.
conclusion: This platform offers a stacking-alignment-independent approach for programmable nanophotonic circuits, but is not aligned with the specified research directions.

title: Exploring Exotic Spin-dependent Interactions Beyond The Standard Model: Theoretical Foundations And Experimental Investigations
authors: L Y Wu And H Yan
abstract: New interactions mediated by novel particles propose solutions to several important questions in modern physics. Axions serve as examples of such particles; they are lightweight and interact weakly with ordinary matter. This category of particles, including those similar to axions—termed axion-like particles (ALPs)—arises from diverse theoretical frameworks, such as the Peccei-Quinn mechanism addressing the strong CP problem, string theory, and spontaneous supersymmetry breaking. Given their light mass and weak coupling, ALPs are also possible candidates for cold dark matter. Introducing these new interactions mediated by novel particles not only tackles several challenges in modern physics but also raises a crucial question: Are there undiscovered interactions beyond the standard model (SM)? Many of the interactions predicted by these theories are spin-dependent, which is the primary focus of this review. In this review, we first outline the theoretical foundations for investigating exotic spin-dependent interactions, highlighting their importance in various models beyond the SM. We examine the potential roles of new lightweight particles in mediating these interactions, which may enhance our understanding of dark matter. Relevant formulas derived from theoretical models are included to support experimental investigations. Following this theoretical framework, we conduct a detailed review of recent experimental efforts to detect these exotic interactions. A systematic review of current constraints on these interactions is presented, along with an assessment of various detection approaches.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to detect exotic spin-dependent interactions beyond the Standard Model, focusing on axion-like particles and their potential as dark matter candidates.
motivation: The paper aims to address open questions in modern physics, such as the strong CP problem and dark matter, by exploring new interactions mediated by lightweight particles.
method: The review outlines theoretical foundations, including relevant formulas, and systematically surveys recent experimental constraints and detection approaches for these interactions.
result: The paper compiles current constraints on exotic spin-dependent interactions and assesses various detection methods, but does not present new experimental data or theoretical breakthroughs.
conclusion: The review highlights the ongoing search for beyond-Standard-Model interactions, emphasizing the importance of spin-dependent probes, but it is primarily a survey rather than a novel contribution to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-spreading Meronic Spin Defects Around Optical Vortices
authors: Miguel A Porras And Yijie Shen Nilo Mata-Cervera
abstract: Optical vortices are singularity lines where the light field intensity vanishes and its phase is undefined. These threads of darkness are adorned by Gauss’s law as lines of pure longitudinal polarization where the polarization plane tilts and winds around. The resulting spin field is as a unique structure with both features of topological texture and defect, as it includes a point defect of undefined spin enclosed by a meronic texture which spans half the spin unit sphere. This topological structure does not spread in propagation: the normalized spin field maintains a deep-subwavelength confinement around the vortex line while the underlying vortex beam continues to diffract. From their intrinsic nature and subwavelength confinement, these textures exhibit enhanced robustness upon isotropic perturbations such as atmospheric turbulence compared with other tailored polarization textures. Here we describe these topologies of transverse spin which decorate the phase singularity of paraxial vortex beams, highlighting the diversity of topological structures that arise in two different spaces—the spin unit sphere and the transverse-axial Poincaré sphere—and discuss the underlying aspects behind their subwavelength localization.
tldr: This paper studies topological spin textures (meronic defects) around optical vortices, focusing on their subwavelength confinement and robustness to turbulence.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize novel topological structures in optical fields, specifically the spin textures decorating phase singularities, and to highlight their potential for robust light structuring.
method: They theoretically analyze paraxial vortex beams, deriving the spin field structure and its topological properties, and compare the robustness of these textures to atmospheric turbulence against other polarization textures.
result: They find that the normalized spin field forms a meronic texture with a point defect, remains deep-subwavelength confined during propagation, and exhibits enhanced robustness to isotropic perturbations.
conclusion: These non-spreading meronic spin defects represent a new class of topological optical structures with potential applications in robust light manipulation and communication.

title: Truncated Differentiation For Inverse Potential MFGs
authors: Siting Liu, Yat Tin Chow, Samy Wu Fung
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study inverse potential mean-field games (MFGs), in which an unknown spatial inverse-cost (mobility) map is inferred from observed population densities. We solve the forward MFG with a preconditioned primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method and develop Jacobian-free backpropagation (JFB-[MATH]), which records only the final [MATH] iterations from a detached warm start while retaining the full forward solve. To analyze this truncated differentiation method, we show that the exact-proximal dual-extrapolated PDHG map is a metric resolvent of the maximal monotone KKT operator. This resolvent view shows that JFB-[MATH] exactly differentiates a finite-trajectory surrogate and, under a locally fixed active set at an exact equilibrium detach point, converges to the implicit gradient as the tracked depth increases. Across several inverse-MFG settings, numerical experiments show that JFB-r at moderate tracked depths can achieve recovery accuracy comparable to full unrolling while reducing memory and runtime.
tldr: This paper develops a truncated differentiation method for solving inverse potential mean-field games, focusing on computational efficiency in optimization.
motivation: The authors aim to efficiently infer unknown spatial mobility maps in mean-field games, which is a challenging inverse problem with high computational cost.
method: They propose Jacobian-free backpropagation with truncated differentiation (JFB-r) that records only the final iterations from a detached warm start, and analyze it via metric resolvent theory of the KKT operator.
result: Numerical experiments show that JFB-r achieves comparable recovery accuracy to full unrolling while reducing memory and runtime.
conclusion: The truncated differentiation method offers a practical trade-off between accuracy and computational resources for inverse MFGs.

title: Robust Watermarks Meet Backdoored Models: Evading Diffusion Semantic Watermarks Via Stealthy Backdoor
authors: Jinyuan Liu, Tianshuo Cong, Pei Li, Tianrui Wang, Xinlei He, Anyu Wang, Xiaoyun Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although semantic watermarking is considered a promising safeguard for images generated by Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs), the reliance of the watermark detection pipeline on neural networks introduces a critical yet underexplored backdoor attack surface. To systematically study this vulnerability, we propose GhostVAE to plant a stealthy backdoor into the encoder of Variational Autoencoder (VAE), enabling reliable evasion of watermark detection. GhostVAE operates in two stages: it first constructs a universal trigger via power spectrum regularization to improve the trigger robustness, and then trains a backdoored VAE encoder with a parameter-aligned objective. Through extensive evaluations across three state-of-the-art semantic watermarking schemes and three widely adopted LDMs, we show that GhostVAE preserves watermark detection performance on benign images (achieving an average true positive rate of 94.4%), while simultaneously enabling highly effective evasion under trigger activation (achieving an average attack success rate of 94.6%). Moreover, we comprehensively analyze seventeen representative defenses and demonstrate that GhostVAE remains stealthy across the input space, parameter space, and latent space. Our work fundamentally undermines the trustworthiness of semantic watermarking systems and highlights that secure deployment of semantic watermarks requires end-to-end security considerations, particularly for neural network components.
tldr: This paper introduces GhostVAE, a backdoor attack on the VAE encoder of latent diffusion models to evade semantic watermark detection.
motivation: Semantic watermarking for AI-generated images relies on neural networks, which are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, threatening the trustworthiness of such safeguards.
method: GhostVAE constructs a universal trigger via power spectrum regularization and trains a backdoored VAE encoder with a parameter-aligned objective to evade watermark detection.
result: GhostVAE preserves watermark detection on benign images (94.4% true positive rate) while achieving 94.6% attack success rate under trigger activation, and remains stealthy against 17 defenses.
conclusion: The work highlights that secure deployment of semantic watermarks requires end-to-end security considerations, as neural network components can be compromised.

title: Explainable Hybrid Feature Selection For Intrusion Detection In Internet Of Medical Things Environments
authors: Amira Berrezzek, Hayet Djellali, Giulio Mallardi, Lamia Mahnane
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) networks are hard to protect: devices are heterogeneous, computing resources are scarce, and traffic must be analyzed in real time. We present an intrusion detection system that addresses these constraints through feature selection. A Pearson correlation filter first removes redundant attributes; a hybrid strategy then combines model-based feature importance with SHAP attribution to pick a compact subset, on which we train Random Forest and LightGBM classifiers. SHAP and LIME explain what each retained feature contributes to the decisions. On CIC-IoMT 2024 and CIC-IDS 2017, the method cuts the feature space by up to 88% - from 40 to as few as 5 features - and accuracy and F1-score stay within a few points of models trained on all features. Compact, interpretable detectors of this kind are practical candidates for deployment on resource-limited medical networks.
tldr: This paper presents an intrusion detection system for IoMT networks using hybrid feature selection with SHAP and LIME explanations.
motivation: IoMT networks are heterogeneous and resource-constrained, requiring efficient and interpretable intrusion detection.
method: The method combines Pearson correlation filtering, model-based feature importance, and SHAP attribution to select a compact feature subset, then trains Random Forest and LightGBM classifiers with SHAP and LIME for explanation.
result: On CIC-IoMT 2024 and CIC-IDS 2017, the method reduces features by up to 88% while maintaining accuracy and F1-score within a few points of full-feature models.
conclusion: Compact, interpretable detectors are practical for deployment on resource-limited medical networks.
